source_text: 53 DE REFUGIS. Damnatorum animae merito se ipsae secernunt; Ex hoc protegenti iterum ad sua recurrunt. Radix Cananaea, maledictum semen, erumpit Et in seruili gente sub barbaro rege refugit, Flamma quos aeterna torquebit die decreto. Uult uagus errare sine disciplina profanus Grassari per fauces uiarum lege solutus. Isti ergo tales, quos nulla poena coegit Si <sece>dere nolunt ab idolis, respui debent.
pass_a_gloss: Damnatorum animae se secernunt; Radix Cananaea/Cain. Flamma aeterna. Without disciplina; if nolunt ab idolis — respui.
pass_b_english: The souls of the damned deservedly separate themselves; from him who shelters them they run back again to what is theirs. The Canaanite root, a cursed seed, breaks out and flees into a servile nation under a barbarian king — those the eternal flame will torment on the decreed day. The profane wants to wander without discipline, to rage through the jaws of the roads loosed from law. Such then are these whom no penalty has forced: if they refuse to withdraw from idols, they ought to be spit out.
